scenes.title: Facebook forms without GoHighLevel
scenes.narration: This lesson connects a Facebook or Instagram Instant Form to Patient Pipeline without Go High Level. We'll use Zapier as the connector and follow one complete route. You do not need to sign up for Go High Level for this method. Facebook Lead Ads on Zapier requires a paid Zapier account, so check your plan first. We'll show each setup step with labeled instructional screen recreations and explain how to verify your own actual submission.

fields.label: Required
fields.value: Paid Zapier access for Facebook Lead Ads

scenes.checkpoint: No current price is promised. Check the plan available in your account.

scenes.title: Before we begin
scenes.narration: Before we start, have your actual offer beside you, and make sure you can sign in to the accounts this lesson uses. You'll need permission to edit the connection. Keep Patient Pipeline open in one browser tab and the other service in another. The little plus sign opens a new tab without closing your work. For testing, use your own name and a phone number you control. Existing emails or texts may run, so let your office know you're doing a setup check. Pause here until you're ready.

fields.label: Account access
fields.value: Patient Pipeline Lead Follow-Up and the source service

fields.label: Test information
fields.value: Your own name and phone; no patient information

scenes.checkpoint: Sign in before continuing. Never show passwords or private links.

scenes.title: Check Page and leads access
scenes.narration: Have the Facebook Page and published Instant Form for this offer ready. The Facebook account you connect must have the Page, ad account, and leads access Zapier needs. If your business has customized leads access, the account owner may need to give Zapier CRM access too. For Instagram, use the Facebook Page linked to the business account. Write down the Page and form names so we can select the correct pair.

fields.label: Access
fields.value: Manage Pages • Manage Ad Account • Leads Access

fields.label: Customized leads access
fields.value: Allow Zapier CRM access when required

scenes.checkpoint: Missing permissions cannot be fixed by choosing a different form.

scenes.title: Open a new campaign
scenes.narration: Let's start in Patient Pipeline. Choose Lead Follow-Up, rather than Reactivation. Then open Campaigns. On the Campaigns page, click New Campaign. A campaign is the offer that brought someone to your practice. We're going to use the same campaign all the way through this lesson, so the connection and the test stay together. Pause here when the new campaign form is open.
scenes.checkpoint: You should be in Lead Follow-Up, with New Campaign open.

scenes.title: Choose the service
scenes.narration: Click Service type to open the list. Choose the service your ad actually promotes. We're choosing Chiropractic for our back pain example. If your offer is for another service, choose that instead. This choice determines which call script your team will use. Check the selected service before moving on. You don't have to copy our example if it doesn't match your practice.
scenes.checkpoint: The selected service must match your ad.

scenes.title: Type a recognizable name
scenes.narration: Now click Campaign name. Give this offer a name your team will recognize. We're typing Back Pain Relief, forty-nine-dollar New Patient Special. You can see the words appearing in the field as we type them. For your campaign, use your own offer name. Keep it specific enough that you can recognize it when we return to check the test.

fields.label: Campaign name
fields.value: Back Pain Relief — $49 New Patient Special

actions.result: Back Pain Relief — $49 New Patient Special

scenes.checkpoint: Use the same campaign for setup, connection, and testing.

scenes.title: Enter what the offer includes
scenes.narration: Under What's included in the offer, enter one item on each line. Our example has a consultation, an examination, and a review of findings. Click the first row and type the first item. Use Add a line for another row, then enter the next item. These details become part of what the caller says, so only include what your ad really promises. Pause and compare your entries with the offer.
scenes.checkpoint: One real included item per row.

scenes.title: Choose Just Y, then type 49
scenes.narration: For our example, we only want to say the offer price. Click the middle choice, Just Y. Then click Offer price and type 49. Look at the On the call preview: it now says Just forty-nine dollars. That's the wording your caller will use. This does not change your software bill. If your ad compares a regular price with the offer, use Normally X, now Y and enter both real prices instead. For this example, we'll keep Just Y.
scenes.checkpoint: Just Y selected • Offer price 49 • Preview Just $49

scenes.title: Save and connect leads
scenes.page: Back Pain Relief — $49 New Patient Special
scenes.narration: Leave the expiration or limited-spots box blank unless your offer really has that restriction. Check your service, campaign name, included items, and price once more. Now click Save and Connect Leads. Wait for the campaign's setup page to open. Saving stores your offer, but it doesn't connect the form by itself. We'll make that connection next. Keep this campaign open in its browser tab.
scenes.checkpoint: Wait until the saved campaign's connection setup opens.

scenes.title: Copy this campaign's address
scenes.narration: In the campaign setup, choose Facebook or Instagram. Find this campaign's private connection address and click its Copy button. Don't copy the ordinary page address from the top of your browser. This special address tells the other service where to send the lead. Keep it private, and don't put it in your ad. We're hiding it in this lesson. You'll paste your own full address into the connection shortly.
scenes.checkpoint: Copy the special campaign address—not the browser's page URL.

scenes.title: Create a Zap and its trigger
scenes.narration: Open Zapier in another browser tab and sign in. Create a new Zap and give it a name such as Send Back Pain Form to Patient Pipeline. Click the Trigger step. Search for Facebook Lead Ads and select that app. For the trigger event, choose New Lead, then continue. A trigger is what starts the instructions. In our case, it's a new submission to the form we're about to select.

fields.label: Zap name
fields.value: Send Back Pain Form to Patient Pipeline

actions.result: Send Back Pain Form to Patient Pipeline

scenes.checkpoint: Trigger app Facebook Lead Ads • event New Lead

scenes.title: Connect the correct Facebook account
scenes.narration: In the trigger's account step, connect your Facebook account, or select the existing connection that owns the right access. Complete Facebook's sign-in and permission prompts in your own account. Never send your password to someone in a message. Return to Zapier and check which account is selected. Then continue to the trigger setup. If your Page is missing later, revisit access rather than selecting a different business by mistake.
scenes.checkpoint: Sign-in screens are not reproduced. Follow the real permission prompts.

scenes.title: Select the Page and exact form
scenes.narration: Open Page and select the Facebook Page for this offer. Next, open Form and choose the exact Instant Form used by the ad. Don't leave the form choice broad if it would send unrelated offers into this campaign. Check both names carefully, then continue to the test step. The next step needs a sample from this form so we can connect its name and phone fields.
scenes.checkpoint: Choose a specific Page AND Form. Generic sample data is not your live test.

scenes.title: Create an identifiable sample
scenes.narration: If Zapier doesn't have a useful sample, open Meta's Lead Ads Testing Tool in another tab. Select the same Page and Form. Click Preview Form, enter your own test details, and complete the form's Next and Submit steps. Close the preview and use Create lead as directed by the tool. Then return to Zapier and click Test trigger. Match the sample's name and phone before you use it for field mapping.
scenes.checkpoint: developers.facebook.com/tools/lead-ads-testing/ • sample only, not live-ad proof.

scenes.title: Find that sample in Zapier
scenes.narration: Back in Zapier, click Test trigger and select the sample that matches the details you just entered. Make sure a usable name and phone are present. If Meta says a test already exists, its Delete lead button removes the tool's sample, not a real production lead. Remove only that test sample if you need to repeat this setup check. Do not delete customer leads to make a tutorial test work.
scenes.checkpoint: Do not use an invented generic sample as evidence of the form connection.

scenes.title: Add Webhooks by Zapier
scenes.narration: Click the plus below the Facebook Lead Ads trigger to add an action. Search for Webhooks by Zapier and select it. For the action event, choose POST, then continue. We're using the ordinary POST action because it gives us simple rows for the information we're sending. Don't choose Custom Request for this lesson. Next, we'll paste the destination and match the form answers.
scenes.checkpoint: Webhooks by Zapier → POST

scenes.title: Paste the URL and choose JSON
scenes.narration: Switch to Patient Pipeline, check your campaign name, and click Copy beside its private connection address. Return to the Zapier tab and click the URL box. Paste with Control V on Windows or Command V on a Mac. Now open Payload Type and select JSON. That is a format choice in the menu; you do not need to write computer code. Leave optional headers and authentication empty for this connection.

fields.label: Headers / authentication
fields.value: Leave empty for this campaign address

scenes.checkpoint: URL from this campaign • Payload Type JSON

scenes.title: Match the name and phone fields
scenes.narration: Under Data, the left side names the information Patient Pipeline expects. The right side must use an answer from the Facebook trigger, not a name or phone you type yourself. In the first left-hand box, type first underscore name. On its right, open the field picker and choose the form's First Name answer. Add another row. Type phone on the left, then choose the form's Phone Number answer on the right. Pause and check both rows.
scenes.checkpoint: Left: first_name / phone • Right: dynamic form answers—not fixed test values.

scenes.title: If your form has only Full Name
scenes.narration: Your form may provide Full Name instead of separate first and last names. In that case, use full underscore name as the left-hand key, and choose the form's Full Name answer on the right. Keep the phone row. Patient Pipeline can split that full name. Use this as an alternative to the first-name row, not a second conflicting name rule. Email is optional; if you include it, select the actual Email answer from the trigger.
scenes.checkpoint: Use either first_name or full_name, according to the fields your form supplies.

scenes.title: Test the sending action
scenes.narration: Continue to the action's test step and send the selected sample. This action test really sends information to the campaign, so use only your approved test details. Check Patient Pipeline for the sample and correct phone. If the action reports an error, check the destination, JSON choice, and mapped name and phone. A successful action test is useful, but it does not yet prove the Zap will run automatically for a new form submission.
scenes.checkpoint: An action test can create a real lead. It is not end-to-end proof.

scenes.title: Publish and turn the Zap on
scenes.narration: Review the Zap from top to bottom. The trigger should be Facebook Lead Ads, New Lead, with your exact Page and Form. The action should be Webhooks by Zapier, POST, with your campaign address and mapped fields. Publish the Zap and check that it's on. The wording of the publish control can vary with the editor. A saved draft is not enough. Once it's active, new matching submissions can be sent automatically.

fields.label: Trigger
fields.value: Facebook Lead Ads • New Lead • exact Page and Form

fields.label: Action
fields.value: Webhooks by Zapier • POST • JSON • mapped fields

scenes.checkpoint: Publish control is illustrative; confirm active status in your actual editor.

scenes.title: Now test a new real submission
scenes.narration: After the Zap is on, submit the actual Instant Form again through the ad using your own name and phone. Don't just rerun the action test. Wait for the form's confirmation, then open Zapier's Zap History and look for this new run. Match its time and form details. After that, check the same campaign in Patient Pipeline. A Meta testing-tool sample is useful for setup, but submitting through the actual ad checks the real route your lead will take.
scenes.checkpoint: New form submission after activation → new Zap run → campaign lead.

scenes.title: Check the receipt, then the lead
scenes.narration: After your real form submission, return to the same campaign in Patient Pipeline. Look for a recent Form submission received message. If it still says it's waiting, give it a moment and refresh the page with your browser's circular-arrow button. Then open this campaign's Leads tab. Match the name and phone you entered. The illustration here is showing where to check, not claiming that a live connection has passed.

fields.label: Latest receipt
fields.value: Waiting for a submission from your form

scenes.checkpoint: No success is assumed. Find your own submission in this campaign.

scenes.title: Recognize a successful repeat test
scenes.narration: For a closer check, open Lead sources and look under Last twenty received. Match the delivery time to your test. New lead means a new entry was created. Updated lead can also be successful: that phone number was already in this campaign. A repeat test may not add another row or move the old one to the top. Rejected means something needs fixing. Open that receipt and read the reason before changing settings.

fields.label: New lead
fields.value: A new campaign lead was created

fields.label: Updated lead
fields.value: Same campaign + same phone may update the existing lead

fields.label: Rejected
fields.value: Open the receipt and read the reason

scenes.checkpoint: Status explanations—not a fabricated delivery log.

scenes.title: Don't mistake an internal test for proof
scenes.page: Only want to check our side?
scenes.narration: There are shortcuts that check only part of the connection. Patient Pipeline's internal test checks its own intake. A connector's test action checks a sending step. Neither proves that a new submission to your actual form will arrive automatically. That's why our final check starts with the form itself and ends with the matching campaign lead. Your test entry is a real lead, so let your caller know which entry was the setup check.

fields.label: Connector action test
fields.value: Can send real data; does not prove the trigger

scenes.checkpoint: Keep private details out of screenshots and shared troubleshooting messages.

scenes.title: If the lead is missing
scenes.narration: If no Zap run appears, check that the Zap is on, the Page and Form are correct, and Facebook leads access is still available. If a run appears but the action failed, open that run and read the error. Check the URL, JSON format, and that the name and phone rows use real trigger answers. If Patient Pipeline says Updated lead, look for the existing entry with that phone. Don't keep making new campaigns to force another test row.

fields.label: No run
fields.value: Check On status, Page, Form, and leads access

fields.label: Failed action
fields.value: Read error; check URL, JSON, and dynamic values

fields.label: Updated lead
fields.value: Find the existing same-phone campaign lead

scenes.checkpoint: Fix the first failing step, then submit the actual form again.

scenes.title: Before you call it ready
scenes.narration: Before you call this ready, check four things. Your campaign matches the offer. Your connection watches the right form and is turned on. You submitted that actual form after turning it on. And your matching test entry appears in this campaign. Leave the connection active, and make sure your team knows which entry was the test. One successful test confirms that delivery; it isn't a guarantee that every future delivery will work. You now know where to check.
